premises.text: Salon and service-space owners cannot efficiently find credible vetted sub-renters via word of mouth or Craigslist, causing high turnover and financial burden
premises.evidence_span: finding sub-renters in a niche vertical remains incredibly inefficient. The only resources are word of mouth and Craigslist

premises.text: Sub-renters need flexible space options across locations and rental durations when clients and leases are geography-bound
premises.evidence_span: due to the inflexibility of rental options, all of her clients alongside her lease were based in New York

premises.text: Renly is a marketplace where owners list space and vetted sub-renters search by industry, profession, location, and hourly-to-monthly rental type
premises.evidence_span: Introducing Renly, a marketplace for renters and sub-renters

premises.text: Supply-side focus across beauty and other service verticals, staying industry-agnostic, drives network effects versus niche competitors
premises.evidence_span: we decided to focus on the supply side because it was the most challenging to scale

premises.text: Renly Circle extends the platform so consumers and professionals discover, book, manage, pay, and provide services in one place including space booking
premises.evidence_span: as a consumer, can discover, book, Manage, pay, or provide any service you want

value.text: Maximize usage of existing service space so owners earn more and professionals work flexibly
value.evidence_span: maximize the usage of existing space

causal_links.evidence_span: optimal solution for both Stephanie, the sub-renter, and my wife, the owner
being industry agnostic is the key to our long-term success

notes: Owner pain (inefficient vetting/turnover) and sub-renter flexibility kept as separately failable sides of the two-sided problem. Listing search facets folded into marketplace mechanism. Listing counts/margins/TAM traction excluded. Renly Circle treated as distinct platform-extension module (v1.3.2 split when framed as second product surface). Not a need/product/money triad: D3 is expansion strategy including Circle.
